findings.headline: The step rate does not collapse AT the handheld profile. It collapses in play mode at every profile, and the handheld profile is the FASTEST of the three measured.
findings.evidence: reports/w1-touch-r2/framerate.json run 1, commit 6bb9003: phone 844x390 dpr3 = 9.04 steps/s at load 2.70; desktop 1280x720 dpr1 = 6.24 steps/s at load 2.81. The desktop null control the critic never took is WORSE than the phone. §4's framing as a handheld problem is wrong; it is a play-mode render problem that touch merely inherits.

findings.headline: The mechanism is the render, and the accumulator is the amplifier. Neither is the touch overlay and neither is device pixel ratio.
findings.evidence: steps_per_raf is EXACTLY 5.000 in every rendering arm at every load — pinned at core/loop.js MAX_CATCHUP. sim_cpu_frac is 0.2-0.4%: the fixed step itself is free. Removing the render (loop.setRenderRate(0), the instrument RI-PLT01 §D M12 says nobody ever uses) takes rAF from 1.0-2.3 Hz to 24-25 Hz, a 16-25x move. Suppressing the touch overlay moves nothing outside noise. dpr 3 -> 1 gave +27% at equal load: real, small, not the cause.

findings.headline: The player-facing defect is not a low frame rate. It is that 87% of simulated time is deleted, so the world runs in slow motion.
findings.evidence: dropped_ms_per_s = 776-882 of every 1000 ms wall clock across all rendering arms; sim_time_ratio 0.07-0.19. RI-PLT01 §C.4 R3 requires exactly this ('max 5 steps, then time is dropped') as a Tier-S structural bar with M8 checking it, so the loop is OBEYING its specification. R3 is written for recovery from a stall; it is being applied to a steady state where every frame is slow, and there it is a permanent 85-93% slow-motion tax. I did NOT change MAX_CATCHUP: 5 is a binding number in a reference item and not a knob a touch round may turn.

findings.headline: This is the cause of §3. The T5 gate's wall-clock length is a direct function of dropped simulated time, not of the gate's units.
findings.evidence: 12 f@60 = 200 ms of thumb time when the sim runs at wall-clock speed. The critic measured 1034 ms because the sim was running at 11.6 steps/s = 19% of wall clock. If simulated time were not being dropped, the gate would cost 200 ms at ANY frame rate and there would be no frames-vs-milliseconds seam to rule on.

findings.headline: My own first control was confounded by load and I am reporting it rather than keeping the number.
findings.evidence: Run 1 took six arms in sequence while load per core drifted 2.70 -> 4.07, and 'the control went red' was partly the box. Run 2 is A-B-A bracketed: four takes of the IDENTICAL phone arm gave 7.83 / 5.14 / 6.00 / 4.00 steps/s — a 66.7% spread with nothing changed. Under bracketing the stall control DID NOT GO RED (7.20 vs a 5.74 baseline mean), because a 60 ms busy-wait against a 640 ms frame is +9% and invisible. That is a weak control, not a passing one. Every cross-arm claim smaller than 67% in this piece is void; A1's desktop/phone gap is at the edge of it and is reported as such; A2's 16-25x norender move is far outside it and stands.

findings.headline: S39's remedy landed and its prediction holds exactly. In mode play at 6 fixed steps/s (10% of real time), presses stamped at 20/60/120/250/500 ms give frames_held 1/4/7/15/30 f@60 and verdicts roll/roll/roll/sprint/sprint.

The delete-the-fix control reproduces the original defect exactly: 5 of 5 roll, frames_held 0 on every row — one constant across a 25x range of thumb time, which is S39's own characterisation of the bug.
M-P5's boundary did not move. touch-run.mjs --leg gate is green on both arms: roll at <= 11 f@60, sprint from 12, identical on touch and pad.

My first rewrite moved M-P5's boundary from 12 to 11 on BOTH paths and --leg gate caught it. A sample taken while the control is still down is inclusive of the press frame; an endpoint at the release is not. Two functions now, framesHeldWhileDown() and framesHeld(), each named for its question.
findings.evidence: the failing run is in reports/runs/_raw/; the fix is the split in game/src/input/hold-gate.js

findings.headline: --leg insets had never run and would have died on its first attempt for a reason unrelated to its measurement: page.screenshot() timed out at 30 s on SwiftShader under load and took the whole leg with it. A picture cannot be allowed to kill a measurement; shot() now has a 120 s budget and records its own failure as data.

The CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) route does not reach TouchInput in a Playwright context: TouchInput.insets reads {0,0,0,0} even with the cutout emulated. The leg forces the insets through setViewport() so T8 clause 1 is tested against a non-zero inset one way or another, but the CSS path itself is UNMEASURED and nothing in the tree measures it.
